title: AFTER - Miro Board

body:
From memory the questions were much simpler: what makes someone human, how much does AI have to become like us before we let it replace things we normally do, and can art reveal parts of someone they cannot directly explain. On the board I made them heavier. That is growth, but it is also something I do. I add clauses until the question can hold everything I am scared of leaving out.

Question 2 is still the one that feels the most mine. The other two feel like they feed into it.

Question 1 asks what there actually is to copy or lose. I used physical, mental and emotional because I needed some structure. I do not think I proved those are the only three things that make a person. They are just broad enough that memory, behaviour, emotion, relationships, decision making and things like that can start being approached without me trying to solve the entire mind body problem.

I am not trying to solve the human being in a paper. I am trying to make something.
That is a difference that matters in this context.

Question 2 is messy because I combined resemblance and delegation in one question. Those might not even require each other. Something does not have to look human for me to give it authority. Google does not look human. Navigation does not look human. A recommendation system does not need a face. So maybe resemblance is not only visual or behavioural. Maybe function can be resemblance too. If it can do the thing I usually do then that might already be enough for comparison.

Question 3 I am still not sure about. It might be the method more than its own research question, and that is not a small difference. If art is the question then I am researching what art reveals about the self. If art is the method then I am using somebody making something as the place where identity and authorship can actually be interfered with. I think I am moving towards the second one, but I do not want to kill the first yet because there is still something interesting about whether people reveal parts of themselves through the choices they make while creating without even noticing it.

The board made one thing clearer though. I am becoming less interested in proving whether AI becomes a human being. I care more about whether humans decide it is close enough to be allowed to do something that used to require them. That is a different  might become a threshold.

What is not up to standard yet is that the three questions still leak into each other. Question 1 and 2 can collapse together if I am not careful and question 3 is doing two jobs. The board is a map, not finished research. It helped me separate the project, but I still need to narrow what each question is actually responsible for.

One sentence from here: Maybe AI does not need to become us. Maybe it only needs us to stop requiring the difference.
